import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_67/test_0.csv"
    ]

    # List to hold transformed DataFrames from each source
    transformed_dfs = []

    for file_path in source_files:
        # Load source data
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

        # Group by user_id and aggregate the relevant columns by mean
        # This converts multiple time entries per user_id into one row per user_id
        agg_df = df.groupby('user_id', as_index=False).agg({
            'sad.depressed': 'mean',
            'open.stressed': 'mean'
        })

        # Rename columns to match target schema
        agg_df.rename(columns={
            'sad.depressed': 'sad',
            'open.stressed': 'stressed'
        }, inplace=True)

        # Ensure correct dtypes
        agg_df['user_id'] = agg_df['user_id'].astype(int)
        agg_df['sad'] = agg_df['sad'].astype(float)
        agg_df['stressed'] = agg_df['stressed'].astype(float)

        transformed_dfs.append(agg_df)

    # Since we have only one source, just take that DataFrame
    # If multiple sources existed, we would concatenate them here
    target_df = pd.concat(transformed_dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # If multiple sources had overlapping user_ids, you might want to aggregate again here.
    # For safety, aggregate again by user_id taking mean of sad and stressed
    target_df = target_df.groupby('user_id', as_index=False).agg({
        'sad': 'mean',
        'stressed': 'mean'
    })

    # Write the final target DataFrame to CSV
    target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_67/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
